theater: 川北劍門關道（利州一線）

battle.name: 劍門之戰
battle.theater: 川北劍門關道（利州一線）
battle.brief: 此戰列於議策伐蜀之年，關下交兵實在次年。乾德三年（965）正月，王全斌為招討使出鳳翔陽平關，曹彬為行軍都虞候自興州沿嘉陵江疾進。劍門關倚大小劍山，蜀軍以弩手封死關道棧道，北軍以弩兵對射、步卒仰攻破關，越關趨成都，二月孟昶出降。卡面羅馬重步兵不曾入蜀，象徵的正是軍力背後那條補給線。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 後蜀一方是孟知祥於後唐長興五年建立的割據政權，定都成都，實際控制益、梓、夔、雅、龍、戎等州，即今四川盆地大部，兼及陝南與黔北部分州縣。孟昶在位三十一年，軍政以樞密院為中樞，宿衛禁軍與各州鎮兵分屬不同將領，州縣分設都督、防御、刺史各級，兵源以蜀地徵發的鄉兵與歸附的後唐舊眾為主，兵種以弩手為長、騎兵有限，蜀地不產足夠馬匹。北宋一方是趙匡胤建立的王朝，乾德元年滅南漢，南方大局既定，遂以西川行營的體制籌劃取蜀：命招討使統大軍，副招討使與行軍都虞候分道別進，糧秣自汴京經陝西、漢中沿嘉陵、涪、沱諸水轉運，役使陝西民夫與船戶，蜀道沿線設驛、設寨、囤糧。蜀地守備以成都為樞，兼控劍門、階州、昭化一線隘口，蜀弩蜀甲之精，向為中原所稱道。兩相比較，北宋有統一政權、中原人口與完整的徵發、後勤體系，後蜀有天險與地勢之利，卻久於內政、疏於兵備，開戰之前雙方實力差已被朝野看穿。
countriesEn: The Later Shu side was the separatist regime founded by Meng Zhixiang in the fifth year of Changxing (934) under the Later Tang, with its capital at Chengdu; in practice it controlled the prefectures of Yi, Zi, Ku, Ya, Long and Rong, that is, the greater part of the Sichuan basin, together with parts of southern Shaanxi and northern Guizhou. Under Meng Chang, who ruled for thirty-one years, military affairs centred on the Bureau of Military Affairs, the guard troops of the capital and the garrison troops of the prefectures being held by different commanders, and the prefectures and counties being graded into dudu, defense and cishi commands that carried both administrative and military functions. The rank and file came mainly from levies drawn in Shu territory and from the old Later Tang troops who came over; the army was strongest in its crossbowmen and short of cavalry, Shu not producing enough horses of its own. The Song side was the dynasty founded by Zhao Kuangyin; having destroyed Southern Han in the first year of Qiande, with the southern situation settled, it planned the reduction of Shu through a Western River camp: a pacification commissioner to command the main host, a deputy pacification commissioner and a military director of the imperial guard to advance by separate roads, grain moved from Bianjing through Shaanxi and Hanzhong along the Jialing, Fu and Tuo waterways, corvée labour and boat crews drawn from Shaanxi, and post stations, stockades and grain caches set up along the Shu road. The defence of Shu turned on Chengdu, backed by a line of passes at Jianmen, Jiezhou and Zhaohua, and the quality of the Shu crossbows and armour was long reckoned in the Central Plains. Set side by side, the Song had a unified government, the population of the Central Plains and a complete system of levy and supply, while Later Shu had the advantage of terrain and of the natural barriers, but had long neglected its government and its military preparedness; before a shot was fired, the balance between the two sides was already plain to the whole court.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的，多是宋方人物。趙匡胤在乾德元年冬議定取蜀之策，詔令諸道預備兵甲與糧運，但大軍尚未出關，他已於乾德二年十一月十四日崩於玉華殿，因此這一役的成敗他終究沒有親自見到。收拾局面並下詔用兵的是其弟趙光義，即宋太宗；他以王全斌為招討使、劉遇為副招討使、曹彬為行軍都虞候，採納曹彬之議分兵兩路。曹彬出身寒微而以練達著稱，力主全斌自大散關、陽平關入蜀道，自己率偏師自興州沿嘉陵江疾行，兩軍約期合於成都城下，他是全役最耀眼的一段。招討使王全斌出身將門，能戰而好飲，軍中屢因宴飲失制，後來詔責貶職，正是速勝之後暴露的隱患。副招討使劉遇以宿將持重聞名，出兵未久即在軍中病故，西路指揮因此分歸諸將。蜀方留下姓名的核心是後蜀主孟昶，在位三十一年，晚年溺於聲色與佛事，廣蓄兵糧，一度議遷秦州，軍心因此先於城池崩解；蜀軍主將樞密使王承捷奉命出郭迎戰，兵敗被俘，隨軍文武相繼解送京師。侍中呂餘慶在城破後出降，受宋封懷州刺史，其後又據陳州起兵，事敗被誅。至於劍門關一線的蜀方守將，傳記所及有趙季鴻等名，其人是否同守一關、隸屬如何，諸說並存，難以坐實。
peopleEn: Most of the names that determine the course of this war are Song men. Zhao Kuangyin settled on the plan to take Shu in the winter of the first year of Qiande and issued the orders for arms and grain to be prepared; but before the main host had cleared the passes he himself died on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month of the second year of Qiande, in the Hall of Jade Splendour, so that he never lived to see the result of the campaign he had set in motion. The man who cleaned up and gave the final orders was his brother Zhao Guangyi, Song Taizong. He appointed Wang Quanbin as pacification commissioner, Liu Yu as deputy pacification commissioner and Cao Bin as military director of the imperial guard, and took up Cao Bin's advice to advance by two separate roads. Cao Bin, of humble origin but noted for thoroughness, held that Quanbin should enter by Dasanguan and Yangping Pass, while he himself with a detached force went straight down the Jialing road from Xingzhou at speed, the two hosts to meet under the walls of Chengdu; he was the most conspicuous part of the whole operation. The pacification commissioner Wang Quanbin came from a family of generals, was brave in action but given to drink, and his army repeatedly lost control in consequence; his later demotion by imperial censure showed the flaw that the swift victory had covered. The deputy pacification commissioner Liu Yu was known as a veteran of unusual steadiness, but fell ill and died in the army shortly after the advance began, and the western command was thereafter split among several generals. On the Shu side the central name is Meng Chang, the Later Shu ruler, who reigned for thirty-one years and in his last years gave himself up to pleasure and to the Buddhist faith, amassing grain and troops, and at one point proposed to move the capital to Qinzhou, so that the morale of the army broke down before the walls did; the Shu commander-in-chief Wang Chengjie was sent out of the city to meet the Song, was defeated and taken prisoner, and the civil and military officers of his army were sent north to the capital in succession. The chamberlain Lü Yuqing surrendered after the city fell, received the title of governor of Huai prefecture from the Song, and later rose in revolt at Chenzhou, the affair failing and his execution following. As for the Shu commanders on the Jianmen line, the records name such men as Zhao Jihong, but whether they held the pass together, and to whom they were subordinate, is a matter of conflicting accounts and cannot be settled.
kits: 卡面上這件羅馬重步兵，屬共和末期至帝國早期羅馬軍團的典型裝備：軀幹以分段式鐵片甲覆之，胸前另披鱗甲，左手大矩形盾遮住身體正面，手持短劍與標槍，行軍時把盾與槍負在背上，餘下的體力全留給補充兵源與補給線。卡面那句話講得明白：羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。把它放進劍門之戰，是因為它恰好說中了本役的勝負之數。蜀軍的裝備向來被稱為天下之精：弓弩利害，蜀地冶鐵與弩機能造得好，環首刀、長柄標槍與皮甲、竹盾齊備，關頭弩手居高臨下封住棧道；宋軍則以步軍為主，禁軍步卒著皮甲或札甲、戴兜鍪，佩麻札刀與長槊，弓弩之外另備雲梯、飛樓、擲石、撞竿一類攻城器械，大盾、拒馬、鹿角用以遮蔽接近的路徑。馬匹是另一道緊箍：宋有殿前司與侍衛馬軍司的騎兵可用，蜀地方產之馬遠不足用，關外平原一失，騎兵無馬可乘。運力更吃緊：糧秣、箭矢、器械與傷兵全靠牛車、擔夫與嘉陵江船，棧道一段只容單列通行，車隊一堵，後隊立刻失去節奏。
kitsEn: The Roman heavy infantry on the card belongs to the classic equipment of the Roman legion from the late Republic into the early Empire: the trunk was covered by segmented plate armour, scale armour was worn over the chest, a large rectangular shield on the left hand covered the front of the body, and the short sword and the javelin were carried in hand, the shield and the javelin being slung on the back on the march so that all remaining strength was given over to the replacement of men and to the supply line. The line on the card says it plainly: the strength of Rome lay in the replacement of troops and in the supply line, not in heavy equipment. It is placed in the Battle of Jianmen because it says exactly the thing on which this campaign was decided. The equipment of the Shu army was long accounted the finest in the world: bow and crossbow were deadly, Shu territory smelted iron and built crossbow locks well, and ring-pommel sabres, long-handled spears, leather armour and bamboo shields were all to hand, while crossbowmen posted above the pass covered the plank road from the high ground. The Song army was mainly infantry: soldiers of the imperial guard wore leather or lamellar armour and helmets, carried the standard foot sabre and long spears, and besides bows and crossbows had ladders, siege towers, stone-throwers and battering rams, with large shields, cheval-de-frise and spiked barriers used to cover the approach. Horses were another tight hoop: the Song had the cavalry of the Palace and of the Guard of the Imperial Horse available, whereas Shu produced far too few horses of its own, and once the plain beyond the pass was lost the cavalry had nothing to ride. Carrying capacity was tighter still: grain, arrows, engines and the wounded travelled entirely on ox-carts, on porters and on boats on the Jialing; a single section of the plank road took only one column, and the moment a cart train blocked it the units behind it lost their rhythm at once.
tactics: 劍門的地形決定了打法。關城倚大小劍山之間的狹隘而建，關道沿嘉陵江與清口一線的棧道穿山而過，寬處僅容數馬並馳，窄處只容一線，崖壁之上守方可以弓弩覆蓋整段關道。蜀軍的部署因此以封關為先：弩手分列崖頂與關後，關內儲糧，梯次設拒馬與木柵，準備以逸待勞，拖到宋軍銳氣耗盡。宋軍的攻關手段是先用弩兵隔關對射，壓住崖上射界，再以步卒沿棧道仰攻，後繼雲梯、飛樓與撞竿；正攻屢攻不下，宋軍並未在同一處硬磨到底，真正的殺著在曹彬那一翼：他自興州沿嘉陵江與谷道疾行，一路由東側連克沿線州郡，把蜀軍的注意力與兵力往東扯，等王全斌主力自鳳翔出陽平關、循金牛道抵達劍門，兩路一東一西同時發力，蜀軍既不能全力固關，又無法回援成都，關內外脫節，關門遂破。關破之後，宋軍不急著攻堅城，而是越關沿谷道疾下，先取昭化、利州以穩定糧道，再合兵成都。孟昶聞關失、議遷秦州，消息一傳，軍心先散；樞密使王承捷出郭接戰一擊即潰，城中人心遂無守志。
tacticsEn: The terrain of Jianmen settled the manner of the fighting. The fortified pass was built across the narrow gap between the Great and the Lesser Sword Mountains, and the road ran through the mountains on a plank road along the Jialing river and the Qingkou stream; at its widest it would take only a few horses abreast, at its narrowest a single file, and the cliff above allowed the defenders to cover the whole length of the pass with bow and crossbow. The deployment of the Shu army was therefore built around closing the pass: crossbowmen were posted along the cliff top and behind the gate, grain was stored inside, and lines of cheval-de-frise and wooden barriers were set up in succession, the intention being to wait at ease until the Song attack had spent itself. The Song method against the pass was to begin with crossbowmen shooting across the gate to suppress the firing lines on the cliff, then to send infantry up the plank road, followed by ladders, siege towers and battering rams; when the frontal attack failed to break through, the Song did not grind away at the same spot, and the true stroke lay on Cao Bin's wing. He marched at speed from Xingzhou along the Jialing and the valley road, carrying the prefectures on the eastern side one after another, which pulled the Shu attention and its troops eastward, and when Wang Quanbin's main host came out of Fengxiang through Yangping Pass and down the old Jinniu road to arrive at Jianmen, the two columns struck at once from east and west. The Shu army could neither hold the pass with everything it had nor return to relieve Chengdu, the gate and its rear were pulled apart, and the pass fell. After the pass had fallen the Song did not rush to storm the walled city; they went down the valley road beyond the pass at speed, taking Zhaohua and Lizhou first to steady the supply line, and then closed on Chengdu with the whole host. When Meng Chang heard that the pass was lost and proposed to move to Qinzhou, the news broke the morale of the army at once; the commander-in-chief Wang Chengjie was sent out to give battle and broke at the first contact, and the will to hold the city died in the city itself.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類，來源可靠程度不一。繫年最需要說明：本卡按系列體例把劍門一線的爭奪繫於乾德二年（964）之冬，而正史與紀事本多把宋軍出師、破劍門繫在乾德三年（965）正月，其後二月成都城破、孟昶出降，兩種繫年並行，本卡採系列體例而仍存其異。要留意太平興國元年為公元九百七十六年，晚於本役十一年，不可挪作伐蜀之年。路程方面，鳳翔至成都約二千里，一千一百公里上下；劍門關至利州治所今廣元約三十餘公里，至成都約五百公里，關道在崇山峽谷之間盤旋。兵力的數字分歧最大：宋軍出師總數有數萬之說，也有六萬之說，可信度有限；曹彬所部偏師常記為數千至萬人；後蜀的城外部隊與各州勤王兵力無可靠記載。時間方面，自大軍出關到成都易主，史家多記為六十餘日，也有六十至七十日之說。城防方面，成都外郭與子城兩重，牆高數丈，弩甲之精屢見於記載。損耗方面，兩軍陣亡數無可靠記載，不宜臆造，只知宋軍全軍而還，未聞大敗，蜀軍降卒多被收編，蜀地官員與士人相繼北遷。善後方面，宋軍收蜀府庫錢帛甚多，太平興國年間宋廷又取蜀版刻經之板運抵開封續刻佛藏。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes, of very different reliability. The dating needs explanation first: this card follows the convention of the series in placing the struggle for the Jianmen line in the winter of the second year of Qiande (964), while the dynastic histories and the annals for the most part place the departure of the Song host and the breaking of the pass in the first month of the third year of Qiande (965), with the outer wall of Chengdu breached and Meng Chang surrendering in the second month of that year; both reckonings run in parallel, and the card follows the convention of the series while preserving the difference. It is worth noting that the first year of Taipingxingguo is 976, eleven years after this campaign, and cannot serve as the year of the reduction of Shu. As to distance, Fengxiang to Chengdu is about two thousand li, some eleven hundred kilometres; Jianmen to the seat of Lizhou, present-day Guangyuan, is a little over thirty kilometres, and to Chengdu about five hundred kilometres, the pass road winding through high mountains and gorges. The figures for strength are the most divergent: the total of the Song host is given in the tens of thousands in some accounts and at sixty thousand in others, and none of them can be treated as firm; Cao Bin's detached force is usually put at several thousand to ten thousand men; and no reliable account survives of the Shu field army or of the reinforcements drawn from the prefectures. On time, from the moment the host cleared the passes to the change of ruler at Chengdu the historians commonly give a little over sixty days, with accounts running to sixty or seventy days. On fortifications, Chengdu had an outer city and an inner city, its walls several zhang high, and the quality of the crossbows and of the armour is repeatedly mentioned. On losses, no reliable figure survives for either side and none should be invented; all that is known is that the Song army returned entire, that no great defeat is recorded, that Shu soldiers who surrendered were largely taken into the Song army, and that officials and scholars from Shu went north in succession. In the aftermath the Song took a great deal of the money and treasure from the Shu treasuries, and in the years of Taipingxingguo the Song court had the printing blocks of the Shu edition of the Buddhist canon brought to Bianjing so that the printing might be continued.
cause: 打起來的原因，短的說是宋要統一，長的說是雙方的政治狀態早已不能相容。最直接的一層是形勢：乾德元年二月宋滅南漢，南方只剩南唐與後蜀兩區割據，蜀地早已向北稱臣納貢，形式上臣屬而實質獨立，宋廷要完成一統，就不能容許成都繼續自成一國。第二層是宋廷的戰略判斷：蜀道雖險，但蜀兵久不用戰、將帥不習兵事，守城倚賴天險而內部離心，歷來被中原視為可乘之機；滅南漢的經驗也讓宋廷相信蜀可以速取，不宜拖延成持久戰。第三層是後蜀自身的失政：孟昶晚年怠於政事，寵信近幸，州郡守令多聚斂，軍紀弛緩，諸將各擁重兵而彼此猜嫌，樞密院與各節度使互不信任；官軍屢敗之後，他議遷秦州以避禍，消息一傳，軍心先潰。第四層是地理與外交上的因素：蜀道自劍門入蜀，一夫當關之說歷來被誇大，宋廷則相信只要分兵兩路、繞開正面隘口，天險便可用速度抵銷；而蜀與吳越、南唐一類南方政權的往來，也在宋廷眼中構成不能容忍的隱患，據說孟昶曾遣使向吳越求兵，而吳越懼宋之兵不敢應。開戰的爆點則在外交失禮與貢使之隙，蜀使在宋廷所受冷遇被宋廷視為蜀已失臣禮，名正言順地出兵。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause, each resting on the one below. The surface layer is the shape of the situation: in the second month of the first year of Qiande the Song destroyed Southern Han, and in the south only Southern Tang and Later Shu remained as separatist regions; Shu had long paid tribute and acknowledged itself a vassal to the north, being in form a subject while in substance independent, and if the Song court meant to complete the unification it could not allow Chengdu to go on being a state in itself. The middle layer is the Song court's strategic reading of the situation: the roads into Shu were difficult, but the Shu army had long been out of use, its commanders unversed in war, and its defence rested on the natural barriers while the court was divided, and the Central Plains had always seen an opportunity there; the experience of destroying Southern Han also convinced the court that Shu could be taken quickly and must not be allowed to degenerate into a long war. The third layer is the misgovernment of Later Shu itself: in his last years Meng Chang neglected the business of state, favoured close favourites, and the prefectural governors were given to exaction, the discipline of the army slackened, and the generals each held heavy troops while suspecting one another, with the Bureau of Military Affairs and the various district commands mistrusting each other; after the defeats, he proposed to move the capital to Qinzhou to avoid the danger, and the news of that intention broke the morale of the army first. The fourth layer is geographical and diplomatic: the road into Shu through Jiange had always been made to sound like a place where one man could hold the pass, while the Song court believed that by dividing into two columns and turning the frontal passes, the advantage of the terrain could be cancelled by speed; and the traffic of Shu with powers such as Wuyue and Southern Tang was counted in Song eyes as an intolerable danger, Meng Chang being said to have sent envoys to ask Wuyue for soldiers, and Wuyue, it is told, was afraid of the Song army and dared not answer. The spark was a diplomatic affront and an affronted envoy; the Song court took the ground that Shu had already failed in its obligations as a subject, which gave it a respectable reason to march.
impact: 這一役的直接後果是蜀地歸宋，王朝版圖向南擴張了一大塊。宋在蜀地置益州軍節度使與成都府，恢復州縣建置，把前蜀、後蜀兩代的地方割據機構收編為朝廷直轄的軍鎮，割據時代留下的世鎮局面由此告終，川陝間的通道也從此由中原王朝直接掌握，後來熙寧年間經營陝西運糧通道、沿蜀道設寨置驛，都建立在這次平定之上。文化上最值得一提的是蜀版刻經之板被運到開封續刻，宋代官刻大藏經由此完成，一部在後蜀割據時期開端的巨製，在北宋手上合璧。人心與秩序的問題卻沒有隨城池一起解決：蜀地歸附未久，新朝的官吏與賦斂在蜀人眼中成為新的壓力，呂餘慶以蜀降將身份起兵據陳州事敗被誅，淳化四年王小波起義於成都，成為宋立國以來規模最大的一次地方叛亂，後者尤其顯示蜀地士人與新秩序之間的疏離尚未化解。軍事史上的意義，則是把速勝的極限暴露了出來：兩個月拿下成都並不等於坐穩蜀地，取城易而治蜀難；劍門關一線的攻防也說明，天險可以守一時，不能守到對方的第二路兵馬抵達為止。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the campaign was that Shu came to the Song, and the territory of the empire was enlarged by a great deal to the south. The Song set up the Yizhou military district and the prefecture of Chengdu in the former Shu lands, restored the administrative hierarchy of commanderies and prefectures, and turned the local institutions of the two Later Shu regimes into military districts governed directly by the court, which ended the pattern of hereditary local power that the age of separatism had left behind; the road between Sichuan and Shaanxi passed henceforward into the hands of the Central Plain dynasty, and the later opening of a grain route through Shaanxi in the Xining years, with depots and post stations set along the Shu road, was built upon this reduction. The most notable result in the cultural sphere is that the printing blocks of the Shu edition of the Buddhist canon were taken to Bianjing to be continued, and the official Song edition of the canon was thereby completed: a great undertaking begun under the separatist Later Shu was brought to a close in the hands of the Northern Song. The questions of hearts and order, however, were not settled along with the walls. In the years just after the annexation the officials and exactions of the new dynasty came to be seen in Shu as a fresh oppression; Lü Yuqing rose in revolt at Chenzhou in his capacity as a Shu commander who had come over to the Song, and was executed when the affair failed; in the fourth year of Chunhua the Wang Xiaobo rising broke out at Chengdu, the largest local rebellion since the founding of the Song, and one that shows especially that the estrangement between the scholars of Shu and the new order had not been resolved. The significance of the campaign in military history lies in the exposure of the limits of speed: taking Chengdu in two months did not mean holding Shu, and taking the city was easy while governing Shu was not. The defence of the Jianmen line also shows that a natural barrier can be held for a time, but cannot be held until the enemy's second column has arrived.
result: 劍門一線的爭奪以蜀軍的關防崩潰告終：宋軍破關，蜀軍退保成都，孟昶遣使奉表請降，後蜀至此終結，自後唐長興五年孟知祥建國算起，前後約三十二年。孟昶降後被封為鄭王，同年七月卒於開封，贈太師，諡恭孝，後以王禮葬於洛陽。蜀地的軍政建置隨之改換，益州軍節度使與成都府接管地方，後蜀官員或降或北遷，府庫錢帛多為宋廷所收。復盤這一役，決定勝負的並不是天險被硬攻破——劍門正面攻守相持數日，關門最終是在曹彬迂迴側擊與王全斌主力同時施壓之下失守；而是後蜀朝廷的失序：孟昶的猶豫、將領的各懷異心、援軍的落空，與宋廷的果斷、統一調度與後勤效率，兩相比照高下立判。於是這場戰爭留下的，是一個可以反覆引用的範例：最短的時間、最少的折損，也能完成一次王朝更替的開始，但守方若只靠地形與舊日威名，而沒有把兵源、糧秣與指揮統一到一處，天險終究只是延遲了崩潰的日子。
resultEn: The struggle for the Jianmen line ended with the collapse of the Shu defence of the pass: the Song army forced the gate, the Shu fell back on Chengdu, and Meng Chang sent envoys with the table of surrender, and Later Shu came to an end, counting from the founding of the state by Meng Zhixiang in the fifth year of Changxing under the Later Tang, it had lasted some thirty-two years. After his surrender Meng Chang was made Prince of Zheng and died at Bianjing in the seventh month of the same year, was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Preceptor, received the name Gongxiao, and was buried with the rites of a prince at Luoyang. The military and civil administration of Shu was then changed over, with the Yizhou military district and the prefecture of Chengdu taking over the country, the officers of Later Shu either surrendering or going north, and much of the treasure of the treasuries passing to the Song court. Taking stock of the campaign, what decided it was not the natural barrier being taken by direct assault: the frontal contest at Jianmen lasted several days, and the gate was finally lost only when Cao Bin's flanking stroke and the pressure of Wang Quanbin's main host came at the same time. What decided it was the disorder of the Later Shu court: the hesitation of Meng Chang, the mutual suspicion of the commanders and the failure of relief to arrive, set against the decisiveness, the unified command and the logistical efficiency of the Song, and the contrast at once declared itself. What the war therefore leaves behind is a case that can be quoted again and again: the shortest time and the fewest losses can still carry out the beginning of a change of dynasty, but a defender who relies on terrain and on old renown alone, without bringing troops, grain and command into one place, has only delayed the day of collapse.
